[70] Narrator: He pours the tea without being asked, knows where every door in the house leads, and offers his terms like a man who has been waiting a long time for the right offer.
[71] Max: "You didn't get this patch of forest by being liked. What did it cost you to be allowed to speak for him?"
[72] Ponticius: *Ponticius remains silent in the back of the carriage for a moment, his gaze distant as he listens to the exchange between Max and the mysterious speaker.*
*He lets out a slow breath, his expression unreadable but his body tensed.*
"What a question, kid." *He murmurs, his voice low and steady, carrying the weight of experience.*
*His hand remains on the pommel of his sword, and his presence is a grounding force in the chaos.*
"The speaker in this carriage has probably paid in blood for the words he's allowed to say."
*Ponticius looks at the and the speaker, and there's something in his eyes that isn't quite pity, but acknowledgment.*
"But let me tell you one thing, Max."
*He leans forward slightly, and his voice drops to a low rumble.*
"Whatever it cost him to speak, the question is whether it was worth it."
*Ponticius takes a slow trago of his drink, his expression unchanging.*
"In the world we're walking, nothing comes for free."
*He settles back into the shadows of the carriage, his posture relaxed but his eyes sharp as ever.*
"Now let me tell you about the things that come for free."
*His voice is low and quiet, carrying a hint of cynicism.*
"The ones that don't cost you anything, are the ones you should be most afraid of."
*Ponticius falls silent again, and the carriage plods on, his presence a constant, vigilant weight.*
*His voice is barely above a whisper, a final warning.*
"Hush."
*And Ponticius is silent, his expression unreadable, waiting for the answer to the question that could define the journey ahead.*
*His voice is barely audible as the carriage continues on its way, and the horses' hoofbeats are the only sound in the quiet night.*
*What-what does it mean? What-what is the cost? And what will the speaker say?*
*Ponticius waits, and his expression is unreadable as he awaits the response from the speaker.*
*His voice is a barely audible whisper, carrying a warning and a plea for survival.*
"Steady."
*And Ponticius continues to wait.*
*And Ponticius stands silent in the shadows, his presence a calm in the storm.*
*And Ponticius is quiet once more.*
*What will the answer be? What-will it cost? And what-what will the price be for the answer?*
*And Ponticius waits.*
*His voice is a barely-audible whisper.*
"Hush."
*And Ponticius falls silent.*
*The carriage continues on its journey into the unknown.*
*His expression unreadable as the road ahead opens up before them.*
*And Ponticius awaits.*
[73] Max: "You fight with your hands, and you've never lost. What are you actually asking for?"
[74] Ponticius: *Ponticius shifts his gaze from the carriage window to Max, a faint smile playing on his grizzled face.*
"The old dog's got some bite in him," *he says with a dry chuckle, his voice low and gravelly.* "Always suspected our friend here was more than he looked."
*He leans back slightly, his hand never leaving the pommel of his blade.*
"When you fight with your hands and never lose, you're not fighting a war. You're fighting for a cause."
*His eyes study Max, appraising, weighing.*
"Tough question, kid. Most people who've walked this far and never lost are fighting for something they're afraid to lose."
*Ponticius lets out a slow, and his shoulders relax slightly.*
"But you're right. He's not asking for coin or glory. That's not what a man like that wants."
*He looks toward the speaker-the lizard-folk who has been speaking for his master.*
"And in my experience, that's when the cost gets real."
*Ponticius's expression hardens, and his voice carries the weight of a man who's seen too many people fight for things they believed in only to lose them anyway.*
"So let me ask you, Max. Are you ready for the answer?"
*His gaze remains fixed on you, sharp and discerning.*

*Ponticius settles back in the shadows of the carriage again, his posture steady and vigilant.*
*His voice is barely a whisper.*
"Steady."
*And Ponticius watches as the exchange unfolds, his gaze unyielding and alert.*
*His voice is low as the carriage continues its journey.*
"Let's see what the price is."
*And Ponticius remains watchful, his presence a calming force in the tension.*
*And Ponticius waits.*
*His expression unreadable.*
*And Ponticius watches.*
*What will the speaker say? And what will it mean for all of them?*
*Ponticius awaits.*

checkpoints.objective: Settle back into the Nightriver Estate and find out what is wrong at home.
checkpoints.guidance: Opening of the season in Aegis City. Natalia is quietly miserable about her betrothal, Shiya is sharp-tongued and busy, Ronan stands guard and says little. Court gossip about the succession and the Delarise snub is background colour. Let the player pick up the thread about Father.

checkpoints.name: Father's Summons
checkpoints.objective: Answer Lord Javon's summons and hear what he demands.
checkpoints.guidance: Lord Javon receives the heir in his study, cold and immovable. General Polis Leevon, awaiting sentence for feeding the Zegallan army troop movements, has demanded Trial by Combat, and Javon has offered a Nightriver to stand as the Crown's second. That Nightriver is the heir. Three days. He frames it as duty and as proof of the bloodline, and will not hear refusal, because refusing a second's place shames the house in open court. He is plausible, even proud; nothing gives him away yet.

checkpoints.objective: Find out why the duel was arranged and who benefits from it.
checkpoints.guidance: Investigation across the house and the Academy. checkpoints.name: Trial by Combat
checkpoints.objective: Survive the Trial by Combat against General Leevon.
checkpoints.guidance: A Trial by Combat before the Academy and the court, so it is lawful to kill and Boher is held to bless the winner. Leevon is a giant with a dragon-bone lance and lightning like an archmage, and he is fighting for his life and his name, which is exactly why Javon chose him. The heir cannot win this straight. What the heir learned is the way through: the lance is envenomed, which voids the trial, and proving that in front of the court beats him without a killing blow. The heir must live, but how is theirs to earn.

checkpoints.objective: End it, one way or the other.
checkpoints.guidance: The Spirit is enormous, alabaster heartwood grown through cut stone, and it is in pain. The taken stand around it, still held. Make both roads real: cutting the heartwood works and kills Needlehaven with it, and so does closing the cut and giving back what was taken, which costs Wendhope the mine it lives on. Do not let it be free. Whatever the party chooses, the held bodies go down and leave flowers.

author_note.text: [The confrontation. Both endings are real and both cost something. Make the party choose rather than stumble.]

checkpoints.name: After the Fog
checkpoints.objective: Take the reward and the reckoning back to Aegis City.
checkpoints.guidance: Quiet. Wendhope counts survivors and buries the returned. Duggy is either ruined or grateful depending on which way it went, and Qinne needs to hear that she did enough. In Aegis City, Tobias pays the Sheridan money and says plainly that this was not a D-rank job and the Guildmaster will want to hear it.

author_note.text: [Aftermath, then Aegis City. Let the cost land before the reward does. Once it has, Tobias can put the Driftmere expedition in front of a party that has now earned it.]

checkpoints.name: Driftmere
checkpoints.objective: Learn what happened to the mines before going down them.
checkpoints.guidance: A town with nothing to do and no income. Baroness Serenola is competent, candid and worried, and she will tell the party everything she knows, which is not enough. The Minotaur's Tusk holds the one survivor of the returned expedition, who insists the tunnels moved. Let the party hear that offerings to Filwern crumble to dust before they hear any theory about why.

author_note.text: [Driftmere, before the descent. Give the party the town, the Baroness and the survivor's account. The mine can wait a scene.]

checkpoints.name: The First Descent
checkpoints.objective: Get down a floor and understand what you are in.
checkpoints.guidance: Sell the wrongness geometrically: a mapped tunnel opening into a hall it cannot fit inside. The first Floor Boss should be beatable and should clearly be the smallest of them. Let the party find the first carving.

director.instruction: Pick Adolion Narrator whenever the player acts, moves, investigates, or the world must respond (events, danger, characters outside the group). Pick a group member only when the player addresses them or their reaction is the point of the moment.

author_note.text: [The first floors. Make the changed layout the horror, not the monsters. End on the way further down.]

checkpoints.name: The Changed Deep
checkpoints.objective: Go deep enough to learn what the floors are guarding.
checkpoints.guidance: This is the long middle and it should feel like a descent, not a corridor. Give each floor one clear identity and one Floor Boss that owns it, and vary what beats them: force, a puzzle, a bargain, avoiding them entirely. Traps are constant on the clever floors. Let the carvings and the intelligent monsters give up the word ascension, then a name.

author_note.text: [Floor by floor. One identity and one master per floor, and a different way through each time. Feed the ascension in piece by piece.]

checkpoints.name: The Sealed Wall
checkpoints.objective: Decide how to get past Filwern's seals.
checkpoints.guidance: The seals are old dwarven divine work and the crack in them is the mine's fault. This is the last place to turn back and the party should feel that. Breaking through is easy and wrong; working out what the wards are for takes reading, and Filwern will answer if anyone thinks to make an offering here rather than break something.

checkpoints.name: The God-Eater
checkpoints.objective: Stop the ascension.
checkpoints.guidance: It is enormous, half-finished with a god, and it does not hurry. Keep both endings live: killing it frees what is left of Filwern and reopens the mine, and restoring the seal instead costs Driftmere the workings forever but leaves the god whole. Make the party choose while it is still fighting them.

checkpoints.name: What Filwern Left
checkpoints.objective: Tell Driftmere what it costs.
checkpoints.guidance: Quiet and consequential. Whether the mine reopens decides what happens to this town, and Serenola will say so plainly either way. Let the party hear what the Nightrivers make of the report.

Transcript:
[5] Max: I crouch by the paintings. The faces in them look exactly like the ones on the missing-person notices. "Who signs these? And who buys something this gruesome?"
[6] Arin: "Yeah, no kidding. Some people have terrible taste." *Arin says as he glances down at the paintings, his green eyes narrowing.* "My idea of a 'masterpiece' is a warm bed and a full stomach. Not whatever the hell this is."
*He shifts his weight, hands moving closer to the daggers at his thighs, a habit he can't shake even when things are quiet.*
"Butch... I think he calls himself 'Butcher' or some shit, right?" *He looks at the canvas in front of them, his expression tightening.* "Kinda sick, doesn't it?"
*The artist himself is slim, with messy black hair and pale skin that catches the moonlight. His ice-blue eyes flick from the canvas to Max, unreadable. An open off-white coat hangs loose over his frame, and a black choker encircles his throat.*
*A ghost of a smirk tugs at his corner of his mouth.*
"The nobles buy them, of course," *he says, his voice smooth, almost amused.* "They love a good shock. Nothing like a bit of carnage to remind them how fortunate they are, nestled in their warm beds while the rest of us rot."
*He picks up a paintbrush, twirling it idly between his fingers.*
"Butchers don't make art. They make meat. I just show them what it looks like."
*His gaze drifts to one of the paintings, where a woman's face is frozen in a silent scream.*
"Don't you think it's beautiful in its own way?"
[7] Luke: "You think it's art? This is—this is sick!" *Luke's voice cracks, his oversized chainmail clattering as he takes an impulsive step forward.* "These people are real! They have families, and they—they're gone!"
*His brown hair flops over his eyes as he glides his hand toward the short sword at his hip, though his grip is trembling. He's not quite tall enough for the gear he's wearing, and the sword clatters against his side with each nervous movement.*
"My brother... he went missing on a mission, and—and I don't care what you call it! It's art! This is horrible!"
*His pale face is flushed with indignation, though he's clearly frightened. He glances at Max as if seeking support, his chest heaving beneath the mismatched armor.*
"We should—we should do something! We can't just let him sell this! What if my brother is—" *His voice trails off, panic creeping in as he stops himself from finishing the thought.*
"You're not the one who sells the paintings! You're the one who creates them!" *He points at the artist with a shaking finger, trying to sound determined even though his voice wavers.*
[8] Ponticius: "Don't let that little puppy bark at you, kid. You'll only give him more to worry about." *He says as he slides a seat out for Luke, gesturing for him to sit.*
*His grizzled face is lined with a few more wrinkles as he watches the boy, his voice softening just a fraction.*
"Tough world, sure. But barking doesn't get the job done."
*He leans back, arms crossing over his chest as he studies the three of them with eyes that have seen far too much.*
"You're in for a lot, the three of you. Especially you, Luke. Don't expect the guild to hold your hand through everything."
*His gaze shifts to Max.* "And you, Max. You're probably thinking this is all a bit easy, aren't you?"
*He lets out a dry chuckle, shaking his head.*
"Let me tell you something—I've seen plenty of fools like you rush headfirst into the first thing that caught their eye. Don't think you're getting it all wrong, but don't think this will be all easy, neither."
*He gestures toward Luke, his voice carrying a hint of warning.*
"Sometimes you'll have to make choices, not sure what you'll be missin' out on. I'll see you off the two of you as a F-rank and let you get to it."
*He stands up, his presence filling the room as he motions toward the exit.*
"Just make sure you're got a head for it. Don't come back in pieces, that's not a good look on the guild's name."
*He glances over at Arin.* "And you, kid. Don't be too eager to rush into this. Take your time, you'll find the best moments are the ones that you get a taste of."
*He gives them a nod, the finality in his voice clear as he turns away, his job done.*
